_note: Source of truth for Google Ads account 788-067-9748. Rebuilt 2026-09-18 from the Keyword Planner data in ads/keyword-research.md, which overturned the first draft: 'crane and rigging services' is 1,600/mo at Low competition and a $3.00 entry bid — three times any other term and among the cheapest — while every medical device term is below Google's reporting floor. Crane leads. Medical runs on a high bid and a small share rather than a big budget. Bidding is Manual CPC because the old account's $1.96 CPC sat below the top-of-page bid on nearly every keyword, which is why 72.8% of impression share was lost to Ad Rank. ads/review.md is the Monday routine that reads this file.

sharedSettings.network: Search only — Display OFF, Search Partners OFF
sharedSettings.locationNote: Presence targeting, NOT presence-or-interest. Same 20 metros as the Google Business Profile. $500/mo spread over 50 states buys about 1% impression share everywhere; concentrated on the densest industrial metros it buys a share worth having. Google's bulk sheet only accepts the canonical 'City, State, United States' form — 'Houston TX' is rejected.
sharedSettings.bidding: Manual CPC, bid set per ad group
sharedSettings.biddingNote: Below ~30 conversions a month the automated strategies have no signal to work with, and Maximize clicks actively misallocates: it buys the cheapest clicks, which is how heavy haul took 74% of spend and returned nothing. Manual CPC per ad group is what stops that without fragmenting the account into campaigns too small to learn from.
sharedSettings.schedule: Monday-Friday 07:00-21:00, account TZ = ET. No weekends.
sharedSettings.scheduleNote: Office hours, not 24/7, and never overnight. The account clock is Eastern and Google applies ONE window to every metro, so 07:00-21:00 ET lands as 7am-9pm Eastern, 6am-8pm Central, 5am-7pm Denver and 4am-6pm Phoenix. Widened from 07:00-19:00 on 2026-09-21 (Sam's call): the old band clipped Phoenix at 4pm local and Denver at 5pm, so the two western metros lost the end of their working day. The cost is an Eastern evening tail and a slightly thinner hourly pace; at this volume the campaigns are impression-limited, not budget-limited, so that is cheap. The early-morning western tail (4am-7am local) is dead air and bills nothing. 22 billable weekdays a month; $25/day lands at ~$550.

campaigns.name: Fleet Dispatch
campaigns.why: Anchored on 'truck dispatch company' — 480/mo at a $1.99 entry bid. 'Dispatch services for trucking companies' is 30/mo at $6.51, sixteen times less volume at three times the price, so it is kept only as a long-tail term. Capped on purpose: dispatch should produce leads without defining the brand.

adGroups.name: Dispatch For Fleets
adGroups.why: The ads do the qualifying, not the website. Copy speaks to multi-truck fleets so single-truck operators self-select out, without the site putting up a wall.
descriptions: US-based dispatch built around fleets of four trucks and up, not single-truck operations.
Our rigging and project work generates the freight. Your trucks run it on real lanes.
A dispatch team with offices and a carrier network behind it, not one person and a laptop.
Tell us your fleet size, equipment and home base. Call, email or send the form.

sharedNegatives._note: Applied to every campaign via a shared list named 'BL - Global Negatives'. Carries the old account's 66 tested negatives plus what the 2026-09-18 autocomplete research surfaced.

neverAdd.free: Blocks 'free quote' and 'free estimate', which are high-intent. Tested and rejected twice on the old account.
neverAdd.ontario: Ontario, California is a major Inland Empire freight hub. Blocking it loses real US shippers.
neverAdd.oilfield: Only ever the phrase "oilfield trucking" — bare 'oilfield' blocks legitimate oilfield rig and equipment rigging work.
neverAdd.badass logistics: Own brand. CTR is roughly 3x campaign average and it feeds Ad Rank. Worth the couple of dollars.
neverAdd.crane rental: Only ever the exact [crane rental]. 'Crane rental with operator' is a service we actually sell, at a $2.35 entry bid.

assets._note: Two sets. The rigging set goes on Crane & Rigging and Machinery & Medical Equipment; the dispatch set goes on Fleet Dispatch, because a trucking company owner does not need a 'Lifts to 200,000+ Lbs' callout — though the rigging sitelinks do quietly make the dispatch pitch, since the rigging work is where the freight comes from.

rules: No prices, no rate claims, no percentages, no MC or DOT numbers, never 'our trucks' or 'our fleet' — the company is not a motor carrier.
No certification claims (OSHA, NCCCO, ASME) unless the company actually holds them.
Freight between sites is always 'through our licensed broker and carrier partners'.

Never say 'heavy machinery movers' or 'heavy equipment' in ad copy — Sam's call 2026-09-18: it reads as heavy haul and trucking, the exact positioning the revamp retired. The keyword "heavy machinery movers" stays as a match target (480/mo) because a keyword never appears in the ad.
Heavy haul is retired. No trailer-type keywords (RGN, lowboy, step deck, conestoga, double drop), no oversize or permit keywords.
Dispatch qualifies for 4+ truck fleets in the AD COPY. The website stays open — no hard refusal of smaller operators on the site itself.
Every quote path is call, email or form. No pricing anywhere.
Stay on Manual CPC until a campaign has 30+ conversions in 30 days, then consider Maximize conversions for that campaign only.
